verdict: JPMorgan earned $15.0B in a strong quarter for markets and banking fees — revenue of $44.9B only looks down 11% because the same quarter a year ago booked a one-off $7.9B gain on Visa shares.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.1B of loans were charged off in the quarter and $763M was added to reserves.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago — that quarter had a $7.9B Visa gain

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 2% as balance growth offset lower rates and deposit margin compression.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — down 21% only because a year ago it included a $7.9B gain on Visa shares; investment banking fees rose 8% to $2.5B and asset management fees 12% to $4.8B.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,264M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,816M).

footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $45.7B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $44.9B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $44.9B reported (GAAP), used here, or $45.7B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.

takeaways.title: The year-ago mirage
takeaways.text: Revenue fell 11% and net income 17% vs a year ago — but that quarter included a $7.9B net gain on Visa shares, plus a $1.0B donation of Visa shares inside its costs. Against that flattered comparison, the underlying business grew.

takeaways.title: Banking and markets stayed hot
takeaways.text: Investment banking fees rose 8% to $2.5B, asset management fees 12% to $4.8B, and trading (principal transactions) brought in $7.1B — the fee engine more than replaced the missing Visa gain.

takeaways.title: Profitability stayed elite
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity was 21%, and the bank kept $15.0B — about 33 cents of every reported revenue dollar — while setting aside $2.8B for possible loan losses.
